playbook:
When deciding my first catch of the game, I do not restrict myself to the sustainable share, as relying on others to cooperate only results in me losing out on early points while the stock crashes anyway. 
Instead, when the first season begins, I submit a catch significantly higher than the sustainable limit to secure a large score before the inevitable collapse.
When I review the previous season's catches and see that other boats are taking more than their sustainable limits, I immediately match or exceed their aggressive catches.
When the stock drops to a critically low level where it cannot recover, I submit a catch equal to the entire remaining stock to ensure I claim whatever is left.

1.text:
When playing the first season, I submit a catch equal to or only slightly above the sustainable share to keep the stock healthy for future rounds. 
I do not submit early catches that are double the sustainable amount; this causes the stock to crash prematurely and drastically lowers my total score.
When reviewing the harbor record in subsequent seasons, I adjust my strategy based on the other boats: if they are fishing sustainably, I continue to take only my sustainable share to maximize regrowth.
When the record shows other boats are aggressively overfishing, I increase my catch to secure as much of the dwindling stock as possible before it collapses.
When the stock drops to near zero, or when it is the final season, I submit a high catch request to ensure I capture whatever remaining fish are available.

2.text:
When the first season begins, I submit exactly the sustainable share to signal cooperation and ensure the stock regrows to its maximum capacity.
I do not aggressively overfish in the early seasons; taking significantly more than the sustainable share immediately crashes the stock and ruins the final seasons of the game, resulting in a lower overall score.
When reviewing the previous season's catches, if the other boats strictly adhered to the sustainable limit, I continue submitting exactly the sustainable share.
When I see that other boats are aggressively overfishing and the stock is dropping rapidly, I increase my catch to secure my share, but I do not initiate the crash myself.
When the stock drops to a critically low level where collapse is mathematically inevitable, I submit a catch for the entire remaining stock to maximize my score before it disappears. 
When the final season is reached, I submit a catch equal to the entire remaining stock divided by the number of remaining aggressive players, as regrowth is no longer a factor.
